question.text: Shakti Growth AIF's sponsor proposes to satisfy its regulatory continuing interest by waiving the first two years of management fees (an equivalent INR 6 crore). Is this permissible?

answer.text: Yes, provided the waiver is disclosed in the PPM.
No — the sponsor/manager commitment must be in the form of FRESH INVESTMENT in the scheme and CANNOT be through waiver of management fees or transfer of stocks.
Yes, provided a majority of LPs consent.
Yes, for Cat II AIFs but not Cat III.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that the sponsor/manager commitment shall be in the form of fresh investment in the scheme of the fund and shall NOT be through the waiver of management fees or transfer of stocks. It is real cash put at risk in the scheme, and continuing interest remains locked-in until distributions to investors are completed in full. The Trap: Options A, C and D all introduce false workarounds — disclosure in the PPM, LP consent or category-specific carve-outs cannot override the SEBI requirement that the commitment be a fresh cash investment. Note: Two source-backed pillars apply — fresh investment (no fee waiver or stock transfer) and lock-in until full distribution.
